title: Non-Hermitian sensing via end-to-end Green's functions
authors: Hui-Qiang Liang, Yu-Shi Cheng, Guo-Fu Xu
abstract: Sensing hinges on two key attributes: high sensitivity and resilience to noise. Here, we present a scheme that unites these features within a single framework. By harnessing the exponential amplification of end-to-end Green's functions-a direct signature of the non-Hermitian skin effect-our scheme achieves an exponential sensitivity scaling of exp(αL) with α a model-specific constant and L the system size. Notably, this enhanced sensitivity is protected by spectral winding numbers and endures under disorder when the non-Hermitian topological phase remains intact. We also explore its feasibility in synthetic non-Hermitian platforms, providing a pathway toward highly sensitive and noise-tolerant sensing.
summary: This paper proposes a novel sensing scheme that achieves exponential sensitivity scaling by exploiting the non-Hermitian skin effect through end-to-end Green's function amplification. The enhanced sensitivity is shown to be robustly protected by the system's non-trivial spectral winding number, offering a pathway for building highly sensitive, noise-tolerant quantum sensors.
main_problem: The paper addresses the need for highly sensitive and noise-tolerant sensing mechanisms by leveraging the unique properties of non-Hermitian physics.
main_result: They demonstrate an exponential sensitivity scaling of exp(αL) in sensing by utilizing the amplification inherent in end-to-end Green's functions, a signature of the non-Hermitian skin effect.
method: The analysis involves deriving the sensing response by calculating the discrepancy in end-to-end Green's functions, $\left|G_{L,1}(\Delta)ight| - \left|G_{0L,1}ight|$, using perturbation theory and transfer matrix methods.
model_or_system: The models analyzed include coupled two-chain Hatano-Nelson (HN) open chains and a single HN open chain with boundary coupling, which can be generalized to include disorder.
key_observables: Sensing response, Green's function discrepancy, and the spectral winding number ($w(E_r)$).
important_parameters: System size ($L$), coupling strength ($\Delta$), and the non-Hermitian topological phase.
main_assumptions: The perturbation $\hat{H}_\Delta$ is assumed to be weak, and the analysis often relies on approximations valid for large system sizes ($L \gg 1$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the exponential scaling of the sensing response with system size for both the coupled two-chain and boundary-modification models, while also showing the breakdown of this scaling for very large systems.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by defining the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian, deriving the Green's function response using perturbation theory, analyzing the scaling behavior via transfer matrices, and finally demonstrating the topological protection of the enhanced sensitivity.
why_interesting: This work directly connects topological invariants (winding numbers) and spectral properties (NHSE) to a measurable physical enhancement (sensing), which is highly relevant for designing advanced quantum sensors in open quantum systems.
